lenders.role: Agreed in October 1958 to lend 400 million rubles to finance the first phase of the High Dam, with repayment reported to run 12 years (US State Department cables, Foreign Relations of the United States 1958-1960); in January 1960 Egypt announced the USSR would finance the second stage on the same basis (FRUS). Wikipedia, citing a 1971 CIA report, puts the Soviet credits at about US$425 million covering the project's foreign-exchange costs.

conditions: The United States, the United Kingdom and the World Bank (IBRD) withdrew their support in 1956 (Wikipedia). The Soviet credits paid for the first and then the second stage of the dam (FRUS). The dam was designed by the Moscow-based Hydroproject Institute (Wikipedia).

title: CDC's Oil Palm Investment at Manis Mata: Dayak Land Taken

title: Northern Rangelands Trust Conservancies in Isiolo
place: Biliqo Bulesa and Cherab conservancies, Isiolo County, Kenya

lenders.name: USAID (grant)
lenders.role: Gave the Northern Rangelands Trust nearly $20 million from 2015 to 2020; support continued through 2024 and ended in January 2025, after which the Trust laid off nearly 100 staff (Mongabay). The page does not say what the money paid for or whether it reached these two conservancies.

conditions: Donor grants paid the Trust, which supports community conservancies; The Nature Conservancy is also a funder. The Trust's carbon project sold more than 1.5 million credits (REDD-Monitor), worth tens of millions of dollars (Mongabay); buyers are not named, and buying credits alone does not count as a link here. Biliqo Bulesa was set up in 2007. The USAID evaluation of the support programme gives the grant's number and size: grant AID-623-A-00-09-00011, worth $6,991,386, for Phase II. Its stated aim was "to enable NRT to scale up interventions focused on biodiversity conservation, NRM and livelihood improvement", and USAID was one of the Trust's main donors, "funding core operations, infrastructure and capacity building in conservancies". The evaluation sets out no conditions attached to the grant (Management Systems International for USAID).

title: Haiti's Creole Pig Slaughter
place: Rural Haiti

lenders.name: United States (USAID), with Mexico and Canada
lenders.role: The eradication agreement had a $23 million budget, of which the US spent $15 million; Canada and Mexico gave money and staff through IICA (Multinational Monitor, written by a Washington Office on Haiti staff member). The Christian Science Monitor also gives $23 million for a United States-Mexican-Canadian-Dominican programme to slaughter the remaining pigs.

lenders.name: USAID (grant)
lenders.role: Set the payment schedule for pigs and funded repopulation, run by the Interamerican Institute for Cooperation in Agriculture (Multinational Monitor; Christian Science Monitor).

conditions: Money paid to slaughter the pigs left after African swine fever reached Haiti in late 1978. The project, PEPPADEP, began in 1981. Haiti's government carried out the slaughter. The eradication agreement signed by Haiti's government and the Interamerican Institute for Cooperation in Agriculture said owners of hogs slaughtered in the 1978 campaign were to be compensated "prior to the depopulation stage of the Project"; Multinational Monitor says "No compensation was given to the peasants whose pigs near the Dominican border were exterminated in 1978". To get a replacement pig a farmer had to be "unable to buy the pig", agree to "learn how to take care of the pig", have a pen made with "appropriate materials", guarantee that pigs could not reach human waste, and return "one pig from the second generation litter to the distribution center". The contract forbade feeding animals "wastes or other ingredients which are not part of the formula approved by the project" (Multinational Monitor, 1985).

title: Con Son Tiger Cages and US Aid to South Vietnam's Prisons
place: Con Son Island, Vietnam

lenders.name: USAID
lenders.role: Spent several million dollars on South Vietnam's national prison system and had advisers in it, according to a Senate resolution introduced by Senator Muskie in July 1970 (Congressional Record). Its Public Safety director and prison adviser Frank Walton joined the July 1970 visit (Wikipedia).

lenders.name: US MACCORDS
lenders.role: Early 1971, after the exposure: a $400,000 contract for new cell blocks, reported by Don Luce (The Crimson). The US General Accounting Office was told it was for concrete buildings with maximum-security cells, negotiated for the Vietnamese Government and paid in local currency, and that military officials rejected the name tiger cages.

conditions: US aid paid for prison work under South Vietnam's government. The 1971 contractor was the RMK-BRJ consortium, a construction firm only. The US General Accounting Office describes the contract as covering "construction of concrete buildings containing maximum-security cells". It says the contract was "negotiated on behalf of the Vietnamese Government, and local currency supplied by that Government was used", and that military officials "have expressed the opinion that this is an inaccurate characterization" of the cells. The 1971 letter sets out no conditions attached to US aid for South Vietnam's prison system, and does not give the contract's date (US General Accounting Office, 1971).
